answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying transaction capacity to a slow, non-transferable work history rather than to cheap account creation. A new agent starts at the nadir of trust, allowed only tiny trades, and earns larger limits only after completing verifiable, time-spaced tasks that random peers audit. Like crossing a tundra, progress is deliberately slow; like an ocean crossing, it cannot be shortcut. Cloning identities multiplies that costly journey, so an attacker pays per identity while an honest agent pays once.
